assertions.text: The skill is described as fully self-contained, bundling the starter template, publish scripts, style guides, and the instructions the AI needs to build websites.
The project is a website template intended to be built and updated through conversation with AI assistants, with users describing changes in their own language and no coding required.

The README lists Node.js and Git as requirements, notes a free hosting account is created only when ready to publish, and says launcher scripts can check for and guide installation of anything missing.
A one-line curl|bash installer places the skill in ~/.claude/skills/ai-website-builder/ and also into ~/.agents/skills/ai-website-builder/ if that directory already exists.
The documented workflow uses two terminals: one runs 'npm run dev' serving a preview at http://localhost:5173, the other starts the AI assistant via npx claude, npx codex, or npx gemini.

A setup.sh script checks the machine, installs the chosen AI CLI(s), completes setup, and provides a quick reference guide; launcher scripts for Windows (.bat), Mac (.app zip), and Linux (.sh) automate the flow including downloading the project and starting the assistant.

Supported AI assistants are Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, and Google Gemini CLI; Gemini has a free tier, while Claude Code requires a Pro subscription or API key and Codex requires ChatGPT Plus or higher.

Publishing is triggered by telling the AI to publish; AGENTS.md maps platforms to npm scripts (publish:github, publish:cloudflare, publish:netlify, publish:vercel) with npm run deploy as an interactive menu fallback.
The template appears to target static sites built with Vite and Tailwind, with publishing oriented toward free static hosts (GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel).

For other tools, users can create tool-specific skills directories (e.g. ~/.agents/skills or ~/.gemini/skills, or project-local .claude/.agents/.cursor skills), or upload a skill ZIP via Claude.ai's Customize > Skills.
builtbyv/ai-website-builder is mentioned in this evidence.
Repository development practice: AGENTS.md forbids publishing without explicit confirmation and requires blocking publication if placeholders or broken essentials exist.

Repository development practice: AGENTS.md requires a pre-publish audit scanning all HTML except setup-guide.html for bracket placeholders, yourwebsite.com, placehold.co, and lorem ipsum, blocking publish until it passes.
Repository development practice: AGENTS.md instructs the assistant to never start background processes, only check whether port 5173 is listening, and ask the user to run npm run dev themselves.

Publishing is triggered by telling the AI to publish; AGENTS.md maps platforms to npm scripts (publish:github, publish:cloudflare, publish:netlify, publish:vercel) with npm run deploy as an interactive menu fallback.
The template appears to target static sites built with Vite and Tailwind, with publishing oriented toward free static hosts (GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel).

Repository development practice: AGENTS.md restricts edits to index.html, additional HTML files, and /public assets, and prohibits editing setup-guide.html, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, README.md, setup.sh, and QUICK_REFERENCE.txt.
